AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does soil conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Covering the soil with plastic
   B. Selling soil to other farmers
   C. Digging up all the soil on a farm
   D. Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place

2. Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bags
   B. Chicken droppings
   C. Fresh grass
   D. Banana peelings

3. Which of these crops can be watered with drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Only trees in forests
   B. Tomatoes in rows
   C. Nothing at all
   D. Only crops under water

4. Where is the neck of the bottle placed in a bottle drip system? (1 mark)
   A. In the bucket
   B. High in a tree
   C. In the soil beside the plant
   D. On the leaves

5. What should you do after the water starts to boil? (1 mark)
   A. Open the pot and blow on it
   B. Add more wood
   C. Add paraffin
   D. Turn the flame down or move wood back

6. What should you do if you smell gas in the kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   B. Switch on many lights
   C. Light a match to see
   D. Cover your nose and cook

7. Which fuel comes in a metal cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Charcoal
   B. Dung cakes
   C. Firewood
   D. Gas

8. Which action wastes fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Turning the flame down after boiling starts
   B. Using a lid
   C. Using dry wood
   D. Boiling water with no lid and a big flame

9. Why do we soak dry beans before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   B. They become bigger than the pot
   C. They become poisonous
   D. They dry out

10. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It gets too hot
   B. The pole is too heavy
   C. It grows
   D. Animals get used to one that never moves

11. Which animal is a domestic animal, not a wild one? (1 mark)
   A. Monkey
   B. Goat
   C. Squirrel
   D. Hare

12. Which part holds the head of the scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. The tin
   B. The top of the pole
   C. The fence
   D. The dry grass on the ground

13. What is biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Only birds
   B. The variety of living things on Earth
   C. Only wild plants
   D. A type of crop

14. Which person is protecting wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   B. A hunter who sets a trap
   C. A person who burns a forest
   D. A person who poisons birds

15. What word means living peacefully together with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Hunting
   B. Trapping
   C. Poaching
   D. Coexisting

16. How do bees and butterflies help crops and fruit trees? (1 mark)
   A. They water the plants
   B. They carry pollen from flower to flower
   C. They dig the soil
   D. They eat the fruit

17. Which tool is used to make the soil fine and level? (1 mark)
   A. Panga
   B. Hammer
   C. Rake
   D. Spade only for cutting trees

18. How far apart may passion fruit plants be planted? (1 mark)
   A. About 2 to 3 metres
   B. 30 metres
   C. Touching
   D. 10 cm

19. Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas? (1 mark)
   A. Cashew nut
   B. Tree tomato
   C. Coconut
   D. Mango

20. What is the purpose of vaccinating animals? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavier
   B. To make them noisy
   C. To colour them
   D. To prevent diseases

21. What is leather made from? (1 mark)
   A. Feathers
   B. Eggs
   C. Animal hides and skins
   D. Wool only

22. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Cow
   C. Dog
   D. Hen

23. Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Protein
   C. Starch only
   D. Sugar only

24. What does variety mean in eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating one food only
   B. Eating a lot
   C. Eating slowly
   D. Eating many different kinds of food

25. Which is a cheap way of getting a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Skip meals
   B. Buy only expensive foods
   C. Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   D. Eat only sweets

26. Which drink is best with meals? (1 mark)
   A. Only soda
   B. Dirty water
   C. Clean water
   D. Only sugary juice

27. Which of these is a kitchen safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Use wet cloths
   B. Never leave cooking food alone
   C. Leave water near hot oil
   D. Play around the stove

28. What should you do before you start cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands
   B. Play with the fire
   C. Eat first
   D. Take off your shoes

29. Why is it a good idea to use the water from boiled vegetables in soup? (1 mark)
   A. It is dirty
   B. It is poisonous
   C. It has no use
   D. It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables

30. Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Mandazi
   B. A fried egg
   C. Chapati in a pan
   D. Fish pieces in a pan

31. What are germs? (1 mark)
   A. Kinds of soap
   B. Tiny living things that can cause disease
   C. Types of food
   D. Large animals

32. What should you use to wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Soap and clean water
   B. Mud
   C. Only dry cloth
   D. Dirty water

33. Why do we dust from high places to low places? (1 mark)
   A. Dust falls downward
   B. High places are easier
   C. It looks better
   D. Low places are dirtier

34. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands with soap
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Play in mud
   D. Wipe them on clothes

35. Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage? (1 mark)
   A. To make noise
   B. To get wet
   C. To be seen
   D. So dirty water does not make a puddle

36. Which kind of PPE is suitable for handling compost? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves and gumboots
   B. Shorts only
   C. A dress only
   D. A necktie

37. Which PPE protects the feet from mud and water? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gumboots
   C. Headgear
   D. Gloves

38. Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust? (1 mark)
   A. Gumboots
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gloves
   D. Headgear

39. Why should tacking thread not be pulled tight? (1 mark)
   A. It will not hold
   B. The cloth will wrinkle
   C. It will become long
   D. Thread is expensive

40. What is a hem? (1 mark)
   A. A needle
   B. A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   C. A button
   D. A hole

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three reasons why PPE should be cleaned. (3 marks)

42. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

43. Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops. (4 marks)

44. List four basic needs of domestic animals. (4 marks)

45. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

46. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)

47. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)

48. State two ways of making drinking water safe. (2 marks)

49. Why must a passion fruit plant have a trellis? (2 marks)

50. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

51. List three safety rules when harvesting fruit. (3 marks)

52. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

53. Give three reasons why a clean home is important. (3 marks)

54. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

55. Explain why a tippy tap is useful in a school without a tap. (3 marks)

56. What is meant by coexisting with wild animals? (2 marks)

57. Explain what thinning is and why it is done. (3 marks)

58. Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community. (5 marks)

59. Describe how to clean gumboots. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Looking after soil so that it stays healthy and stays in place
   Soil conservation protects the soil from being washed away and from losing its plant food.

2. A — Plastic bags
   Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

3. B — Tomatoes in rows
   Drip systems suit row crops such as tomatoes and kale.

4. C — In the soil beside the plant
   The bottle is buried neck down near the plant.

5. D — Turn the flame down or move wood back
   A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

6. A — Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
   Fire near a gas leak can cause an explosion.

7. D — Gas
   LPG gas is stored under pressure in a cylinder.

8. D — Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   Heat escapes without a lid and a big flame.

9. A — They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   Soaked beans soften and cook faster.

10. D — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

11. B — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

12. B — The top of the pole
   The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

13. B — The variety of living things on Earth
   Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

14. A — A learner who reports poaching to a wildlife officer
   Reporting poaching helps protect animals.

15. D — Coexisting
   To coexist is to live together.

16. B — They carry pollen from flower to flower
   Pollination helps fruits and seeds to form.

17. C — Rake
   A rake breaks lumps and levels the bed.

18. A — About 2 to 3 metres
   Give climbers room.

19. B — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

20. D — To prevent diseases
   Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

21. C — Animal hides and skins
   Skins of cattle, goats and sheep become leather.

22. C — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

23. B — Protein
   Eggs are body-building foods.

24. D — Eating many different kinds of food
   Variety means different foods.

25. C — Grow vegetables and fruits at home
   A kitchen garden gives fresh food.

26. C — Clean water
   Water is essential and healthy.

27. B — Never leave cooking food alone
   Careful supervision prevents fires.

28. A — Wash your hands
   Clean hands prevent germs.

29. D — It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   Some vitamins go into the cooking water.

30. A — Mandazi
   Mandazi float in deep oil.

31. B — Tiny living things that can cause disease
   Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

32. A — Soap and clean water
   Soap removes germs.

33. A — Dust falls downward
   Dust moves downward.

34. A — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

35. D — So dirty water does not make a puddle
   Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

36. A — Gloves and gumboots
   They protect hands and feet.

37. B — Gumboots
   Gumboots are waterproof.

38. D — Headgear
   Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

39. B — The cloth will wrinkle
   Loose stitches lie flat.

40. B — A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   A hem stops edges fraying.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can carry germs, it may smell or spoil, and clean PPE lasts longer and protects better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each need.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Its stem is soft and cannot stand, so the trellis supports it as it climbs and spreads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soft stem, 1 mark for support.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a ladder or picking pole; do not climb thin branches; wash hands and fruit; use both hands (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: It prevents diseases, keeps food safe, prevents accidents and looks pleasant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It saves water, it can be made cheaply from a container, and children do not touch the container with dirty hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Living together peacefully so that both farmers and animals are safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for living together, 1 mark for both safe.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
